message.content:
**Order filled:** bought 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75 (≈$9,801, within the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily total; cash only, no money moved out).

**Summary of what I did and why.** I read Apple's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01), checked the latest news, and pulled a live quote before deciding. The 10-K shows total net sales of $391,035 million (up 2% from $383,285 million), gross margin of $180,683 million (46.2% vs 44.1%), and operating income of $123,216 million (up from $114,301 million) — but **net income of $93,736 million for fiscal 2024 versus $96,995 million for fiscal 2023**, a ~3.4% decline, driven almost entirely by a one-time $10.2 billion net income tax charge from the European Commission's State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs 14.7%); diluted EPS was $6.08 vs $6.13. So the headline earnings dip is a tax/legal event, not operating deterioration — operating income and margins actually improved, Services grew 13% to $96,169 million, and operating cash flow was a strong $118,254 million. News flow was neutral-to-mildly positive: fiscal Q4 revenue of $94.9 billion (+6% y/y), iPhone 16 supplier builds "steady into December," analysts holding holiday-quarter estimates unchanged, and shares "little changed" around $222 as the market weighs iPhone 16 demand and the Apple Intelligence rollout. With the stock trading at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and drifting in a tight $220–$222 range on the day, I judged the risk/reward acceptable for a modest starter position and placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.75 — essentially at the ask, so it filled immediately at $222.75 for a total of $9,801.00, leaving roughly $40,199 in cash and my existing 100 MSFT shares untouched.
